rationale: Kept from the revision: five sensors at 0.012 m spacing with 0.016 m footprints, so adjacent sensors overlap and the 0.064 m span covers the 0.025 m tape with margin. Also kept: the axle-relative frame, the body, wheel and mass values, the symmetric weights [-1,-0.5,0,0.5,1] (positive steers left, so the outermost left sensor steers left and the right one steers right), and the 'last_direction' line-loss rule, since at about 0.044 m offset the line is lost before the 0.06 m off-track limit. Accepted from the critique: kd is reduced from 0.5 to 0.3, because the critique is right that derivative action on noisy readings can add large turn spikes at tape edges and at the line-loss transition, and a 1.0 signal jump gives a derivative of about 100 per second. Reduced kp from 6 to 5, since kp times the signal already gives up to 1750 PWM of differential at full signal, and a lower gain reduces the risk of left-right oscillation. Reduced ki from 0.3 to 0.2 to limit integral overshoot after long bends while still allowing about 0.4 turn (about 140 PWM) against the roughly 2 percent motor mismatch. Rejected: the critique's call for a much slower base_speed. A slow run risks failing to finish within 3 s, and completion is worth 500 points, far more than the time term. I keep base_speed at 1.5, but I cannot convert PWM to ground speed from the inputs, so the finish-in-3-s assumption is the main unverified risk. Expected outcome: completion on the development tracks, with rms_error and line_loss_events modest. These are hypotheses to test, not derived values. Fallbacks for the next iteration: if line losses exceed 3 per track, lower base_speed by 0.1; if oscillation is steady and rms_error is high, lower kp by 1; if there is a constant offset, raise ki; if the run stalls or times out before the course is covered, raise base_speed by 0.1. Robustness to the unseen track rests on the overlapping sensors and moderate gains, not on tuning to the development shapes. Tight bends on the unseen track remain the main untested failure mode.
